proof.criterion: The Close and Drain comments are true of the code, including the case the old wording hid.
proof.surface: sessionproxy.go's Close and serve, the connector's Dial (cloud.google.com/go/cloudsqlconn v1.25.4), and close_race_test.go
proof.command: read Close (cancel, then drain timer, then closeConns, then <-drained) and the connector's dial path; ran TestALateDialDuringCloseIsClosedNotCopied
proof.observed: Close cancels the serving context first and then waits on inFlight. A pair already copying is bounded by the drain's force-close, but a serve still inside a dial is only bounded by that dial returning, so a dial that ignores cancellation holds Close until it returns. A dial that ignores its context was driven in round 3's throwaway: with the dial held 100 ms into Close, Close returned at 108-119 ms, i.e. only once the dial was released. TestALateDialDuringCloseIsClosedNotCopied (the same dialer, released as soon as Close marks closing) passes ×3 at this head. The connector honours cancellation: its default dialFunc is x/net proxy.Dial, which dials through net.Dialer.DialContext(ctx), and its TLS step is tlsConn.HandshakeContext(ctx) (dialer.go:233, :636).
proof.negativeControl: the old wording ('never waits on a client longer than Drain') is contradicted by that run: Close's return followed the dial's release, not the drain or the cancellation
